title: The Die-Hard Pour
question: With only a 3-liter and a 5-liter jug and a fountain, isolate exactly 4 liters in the 5-liter jug. How many liters end up there?
correctExplanation: 4 liters: fill 3, pour into 5; fill 3, top up 5 (1 left in 3); empty 5, pour the 1 in; fill 3 and pour — 5 holds 4. Differences stack into targets.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is 4. Fill the 3-jug twice into the 5-jug: the second pour leaves 1 liter stranded, and banking that 1 plus a fresh 3 makes 4. Pour, strand, bank, combine.
lessonContent:
Bank stranded remainders instead of discarding them.
Differences between vessels manufacture new volumes.
Empty and fill are moves, not admissions of failure.
Work backward from the target to the needed remainder.

title: The Beaker Proof
question: A lab holds 4-liter and 9-liter beakers. After a sequence of pours, exactly 6 liters sit in the 9-liter beaker. How many liters?
correctExplanation: 6 liters, built as 4+4−9+4+4−9+4 across six pours with two empties. Repeated small pours accumulate past the big vessel's capacity into remainders.
incorrectExplanation: Close — the answer is 6. Pour 4-liter measures into the 9-beaker repeatedly, emptying at each overflow: strand 3, bank it, strand 2 more against it, and six pours land 6. Count overflows, not just pours.
lessonContent:
Repeated measures accumulate past big capacities.
Overflows are information, not waste.
Track remainders after every single pour.
Small vessels conquer big ones by persistence.

title: The Fuel Depot
question: A depot has 6-liter and 10-liter drums. The attendant isolates fuel in the 10-liter drum using only full, empty, and pour moves. How many liters?
correctExplanation: 8 liters: fill 10, pour 6 out (4 left), empty 6, pour the 4 in, fill 10 and top up the 6 — 2 more go in, leaving 8. Two-stage banking.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is 8. The 4-liter remainder (10−6) gets banked in the small drum, then a fresh 10 minus a 2-liter top-up leaves 8. Bank, refill, subtract.
lessonContent:
Remainders are currency — bank them in small vessels.

title: The Oasis Skins
